Elkhart-based LCI Industries Inc. confirmed Wednesday that it has received an unsolicited proposal by private equity firm Monomoy Capital Partners to acquire LCI.

The proposal comes as the company is set to merge with Elkhart-based Patrick Industries Inc. LCI said in a news release that its existing merger agreement with Patrick remains in place, and the company’s board of directors “continues to recommend in favor of the Patrick transaction.”

However, LCI said as part of its fiduciary duties, its board will carefully evaluate Monomoy’s proposal in consultation with independent financial and legal advisors.

The proposal from Monomoy, headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, involves an acquisition of $101 per share in cash. Based on the amount of outstanding shares of LCI stock as reported in the company’s most recent quarterly earnings, the acquisition could be valued at approximately $2.5 billion.

Patrick Industries said in a statement that it is reaffirming its agreement to merge with LCI.

“Patrick will monitor this development as it continues to execute on its strategy and vision centered around an independent and diversified brand model in the outdoor enthusiast and housing markets,” Patrick said.

Monomoy did not respond to a request from Inside INdiana Business for comment on its proposal.

Patrick and LCI Industries announced their proposed merger in June. Lippert Interim CEO Johnny Sirpilla said following the merger, the company will have more than $8 billion in combined revenue across the outdoor enthusiast, housing, and transportation markets.

The closing of the merger has seen some delays. On Sept. 4, the companies voluntarily withdrew their Hart-Scott-Rodino Act premerger notification forms and refiled them five days later. The refiling initiated a new waiting period under the HSR Act.

On Oct. 9, the companies each received a request for additional information from the U.S. Department of Justice in connection with the DOJ’s review of the merger, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission dated Oct. 13.

Earlier this month, Elkhart-based recreational vehicle manufacturer Thor Industries Inc. expressed concern over the proposed merger, saying warning that further consolidation could increase component costs, reduce competition and add to affordability problems already weighing on RV sales.

An estimated timeline for LCI’s review of Monomoy’s proposal was not provided.
